findings.explanation: Haruki says that he was no good for Kazusa—he was not enough and could not save her. The English instead says he can no longer continue, turning a judgment of his inadequacy into a decision to stop.

findings.highlight: So many things happened, and now I have no choice but to rely on her
findings.evidenceJa: 色々あって、あいつが頼れなくなってしまった…けれど一度は、永遠の友情を誓い合った相手だから。
findings.explanation: Setsuna is the friend Kazusa became unable to rely on after everything that happened, even though they once swore eternal friendship. The English instead says Haruki now has no choice but to rely on Setsuna, reversing both subject and direction.
findings.japanese:
色々あって、あいつが頼れなくなってしまった…
けれど一度は、永遠の友情を誓い合った相手だから。
findings.todokanai: So many things happened, and now I have no choice but to rely on her… but they did once swear eternal friendship to each other.

findings.highlight: the beautiful descendant of a pianist who won a prize at the Giovanni Competition
findings.evidenceJa: 「それで、次の手を模索してたところに出てきたのが、美人二世ピアニストのジェバンニコンクール入賞…」
findings.explanation: The drawcard that appears is Kazusa: a beautiful second-generation pianist who herself placed in the Giovanni Competition. The English grammatically makes her an attractive descendant of some pianist who won the prize.
findings.japanese:
「それで、次の手を模索してたところに出てきたのが、
美人二世ピアニストのジェバンニコンクール入賞…」
findings.todokanai: "And from there, after searching, we ended up chancing upon the beautiful descendant of a pianist who won a prize at the Giovanni Competition…"

findings.highlight: Getting money off fame without doing anything is no different from scamming others.
findings.evidenceJa: 「どこがだよ…腕もないのに人気だけで金を稼ぐなんて、そんなの、詐欺みたいなもんだ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa says earning money from popularity despite lacking ability would be fraudulent, exposing her professional insecurity. 'Without doing anything' instead accuses the hypothetical star of laziness rather than insufficient skill.
findings.japanese:
「どこがだよ…
腕もないのに人気だけで金を稼ぐなんて、
そんなの、詐欺みたいなもんだ」
findings.todokanai: "How exactly…? Getting money off fame without doing anything is no different from scamming others."

findings.highlight: I was simply trying to lighten the mood, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: 「どうかな？ただのウサ晴らしかもしれないよ？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna suggests she may simply be venting her own frustration on Kazusa. The English says she is trying to lighten the mood, reversing a hostile cathartic motive into a benevolent social one.
findings.japanese:
「どうかな？
ただのウサ晴らしかもしれないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "Who knows? I was simply trying to lighten the mood, you know?"
